body:
You hit record sales in December. By the second week of February, your revenue drops to near zero and you start questioning your entire business model.

Business in Nigeria does not respect standard economic principles. When the market goes quiet, most founders panic. They blame their sales team, slash prices, or assume the business is failing.

But here is the reality: you are not failing. You are just fighting a seasonal cycle you have not mapped out.

In the latest episode of the Everything Entrepreneurship Podcast, Sharon Canu and I sat down with Mr. Ek, a veteran entrepreneur with over two decades of experience navigating the Nigerian market—from retail and construction to healthcare.

We broke down the exact commercial calendar of the country.

There are distinct "Boom Windows"—like March to June when government and corporate budgets are released, and the notorious "Dirty December" diaspora rush. But more importantly, there are brutal dry spells. January to February is slow. July to September is tight.

If you do not build operational structure for the dry spells while you are making money in the peak, you will bleed out.

In this episode, we discussed:

The 6-Month Cash Buffer: Why you need to aggressively save 30% to 50% of your peak revenue to fund payroll during the quiet months.

Dry Season Operations: Why slow months are not for panic—they are the time to restructure your internal systems, train your frontline staff, and negotiate supplier credit.

Off-Cycle Marketing: Why checking on your customers when they are not buying guarantees they will spend with you when the market opens back up.

If your business is currently experiencing a slump, do not panic. The money has not disappeared; it is just a different season.
summary:
Every Nigerian business has seasons. The question is whether you're ready for them.


In this episode of Everything Entrepreneurship, we sit down with Mr. Ikenna, a trained pharmacist and Business Development Manager with over two decades of business experience, to break down Nigeria's demand seasons from the inside. We explore why sales slow down when they do, what's actually happening in the market during peak periods, and the moves founders need to make on both sides of the cycle.


Whether you're watching cash bleed in a slow month or trying to maximise a boom, this episode gives you the framework to stop reacting and start planning.


What we cover:

  •  The demand seasons every Nigerian business moves through
  •  Why the dip happens and what it's actually telling you
  •  How to protect your business when sales slow down
  •  How to position and push when peak season hits
  •  Real lessons from over 20 years of operating in the Nigerian market
title: Nigeria's Business Seasons Explained: How to Survive Slow Sales and Win in Peak Season
